recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-29661 unless a future work-group decision changes how Subscription or SubscriptionStatus should model entered-in-error.
issue_request: FHIR-29661 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and asked to add entered-in-error to Subscription.status and SubscriptionStatus.status, with documentation of its use, after validator warnings showed those status elements lacked an entered-in-error value.
initial_application: The Jira snapshot records the issue as applied in commit 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157. That broad source-rework commit introduced XML Subscription and SubscriptionStatus definitions with entered-in-error in status metadata; later source history preserved the value while moving the binding to the current subscription-status terminology.
additional_context: Subscription and SubscriptionStatus are active resources and approved in source/fhir.ini. The current subscription-status CodeSystem defines entered-in-error, the ValueSet includes that CodeSystem, and both Subscription.status and SubscriptionStatus.status bind required to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/subscription-status. Confluence FHIR-I WGM 202101 minutes independently record the FHIR-29661 motion as will fix as suggested with the same 17-0-0 persuasive vote. Later FHIR-35788 renamed the ValueSet to SubscriptionStatusCodes and restored SubscriptionStatus code system naming without changing the entered-in-error semantics.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The current authoritative XML and fhir.ini build configuration already satisfy the Jira request through the status code, required bindings, entered-in-error build metadata, and concise definition text.

related_jiras.note: Renamed the subscription status ValueSet/binding names after FHIR-29661 while preserving the entered-in-error code and semantics.
